_meta.note: RXGUARD_V190_JOINT. Generic label-maximum daily ceilings for pain medicines, for a copy that has no personal dose-rules file (the Family Edition). Pharmacology only: it names no person and says nothing about who takes what. Oral and injected doses count against each NSAID ceiling; a topical gel or patch is shown beside it and never added into it ('routes'). The two class loads count distinct NSAIDs taken by mouth or injection in 24 hours. A personal dose_rules.local.json, when one exists, is used instead of this file.

paracetamol.label: Paracetamol
paracetamol.source: US FDA acetaminophen labelling: maximum 4,000 mg in 24 hours, all products combined.
paracetamol.consequence: Liver injury rises above the daily maximum; combination products are the usual way it is crossed.

ibuprofen.label: Ibuprofen
ibuprofen.source: US prescribing information (ibuprofen tablets): 'Do not exceed 3200 mg total daily dose.'
ibuprofen.consequence: Stomach bleeding, kidney and blood-pressure effects are dose-related.

diclofenac.label: Diclofenac
diclofenac.source: US prescribing information (diclofenac sodium delayed-release), osteoarthritis: 100-150 mg a day in divided doses.
diclofenac.consequence: Stomach bleeding, kidney and cardiovascular effects are dose-related.

aceclofenac.label: Aceclofenac
aceclofenac.source: EU SmPC (aceclofenac 100 mg tablets), 4.2: one tablet twice daily, 200 mg a day.
aceclofenac.consequence: Stomach bleeding, kidney and cardiovascular effects are dose-related.

naproxen.label: Naproxen
naproxen.source: US prescribing information (naproxen): up to 1500 mg a day for limited periods.
naproxen.consequence: Stomach bleeding, kidney and cardiovascular effects are dose-related.

etoricoxib.label: Etoricoxib
etoricoxib.course_note: 120 mg is licensed for acute gout only, for at most 8 days; 60-90 mg a day otherwise.
etoricoxib.source: EU SmPC (etoricoxib), 4.2: osteoarthritis 30-60 mg once daily; 120 mg only in acute gouty arthritis, maximum 8 days.
etoricoxib.consequence: Blood pressure, fluid retention and cardiovascular risk are dose-related.

celecoxib.label: Celecoxib
celecoxib.source: US prescribing information (celecoxib): osteoarthritis 200 mg a day; rheumatoid arthritis up to 200 mg twice daily.
celecoxib.consequence: Cardiovascular and kidney effects are dose-related.

piroxicam.label: Piroxicam
piroxicam.source: US prescribing information (piroxicam): 20 mg a day.
piroxicam.consequence: Stomach bleeding risk is among the highest of the NSAIDs.

etodolac.label: Etodolac
etodolac.source: US prescribing information (etodolac): up to 1000 mg a day.
etodolac.consequence: Stomach bleeding, kidney and cardiovascular effects are dose-related.

ketorolac.label: Ketorolac
ketorolac.course_note: Ketorolac, by any route, for 5 days in total at most.
ketorolac.source: US prescribing information (ketorolac tablets): maximum 40 mg a day by mouth; total duration not to exceed 5 days.
ketorolac.consequence: Stomach bleeding and acute kidney injury rise steeply with dose and duration.

nimesulide.label: Nimesulide
nimesulide.course_note: Nimesulide is limited to 15 days of treatment.
nimesulide.source: EMA (2012) assessment of nimesulide: 100 mg twice daily, treatment no longer than 15 days.

tramadol.label: Tramadol
tramadol.source: US prescribing information (tramadol): 'not to exceed 400 mg/day'.
tramadol.consequence: Seizures, serotonin toxicity, sedation and falls rise with dose.

tapentadol.label: Tapentadol
tapentadol.source: US prescribing information (tapentadol immediate-release): daily doses above 600 mg have not been studied.
tapentadol.consequence: Sedation, breathing depression and falls rise with dose.

codeine.label: Codeine
codeine.source: UK SmPC (codeine phosphate): maximum 240 mg a day.
codeine.consequence: Sedation, constipation and breathing depression rise with dose.

thiocolchicoside.label: Thiocolchicoside
thiocolchicoside.course_note: By mouth, 8 mg every 12 hours for at most 7 days.
thiocolchicoside.source: EMA (2013) restriction of thiocolchicoside: oral 8 mg every 12 hours, no longer than 7 consecutive days.
thiocolchicoside.consequence: Genotoxic metabolite at higher exposure; drowsiness.

classes.label: Stomach-risk load (NSAIDs by mouth or injection)
classes.consequence: Two NSAIDs together add the stomach-bleeding risk without adding pain relief.
classes.action: Take one NSAID only; ask before combining.

classes.label: Kidney-risk load (NSAIDs by mouth or injection)
classes.consequence: NSAIDs reduce kidney blood flow; more than one at a time, or with a water tablet or blood-pressure tablet of the ACE/ARB kind, adds to it.
classes.action: One NSAID at a time, drink enough, and have kidney function checked if they are taken for more than a few days.
